newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish share index rises in shipper Moeller's wake.
newsitem.headline: Danish share index rises in shipper Moeller's wake.

text.p: Danish share prices rose in defiance of expectations on Tuesday, propelled mainly by keen interest in shipping heavyweight A.P. Moeller, with help from biotech group Novo Nordisk and telecoms group Tele Danmark.
"We had a positive day, primarily due to new buying in the A.P. Moeller companies," a dealer said, adding that he expected to see the KFX top-20 index gain another 0.5 to 1.0 point on Wednesday.
The index closed 1.28 point up, at 154.74, in modest overall bourse turnover of 698 million crowns. Its June future rose 0.65 point to 153.20 with 120 contracts, each of 100,000-crowns, traded.
A.P. Moeller's D/S 1912 rose 2,500 crowns to 203,500 and its D/S Svendborg climbed the same amount to 294,000 crowns.
Novo Nordisk rose 10 crowns to 669 crowns and Tele Danmark put on nine crowns to end at 335, clawing back much of its 11-crown loss from Monday's profit warning.

The 51 percent state-owned Tele Danmark on Tuesday issued a new statement saying that losses resulting from new regulatory proposals would be less than previously thought. The news came after the market closed but had been widely anticipated.
